chapter: Learning from Fletcher's circle in New York
title: What school gave him versus learning in New York
summary: School gave a foundation, but his real education came from asking the giants of jazz in New York, including the jam sessions at Coleman Hawkins' place.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: That's great. Do you feel that the musical training you had in the school helped you with what you were doing or did you find it at odds, or how do you feel about that?

It did give me the foundation, Tom, a little bit, you know, but my greatest experience came from being in New York, seeing these giants of jazz execute it, and being able to ask them questions and them givin' me the correct answer. There weren't too many books out, as you know, during that time like they are now. So this came from, as we say, the horse's mouth. And these guys would tell you just exactly how it is and how it was done. Plus the fact -- I will inject this here -- I remember when we had dinner a couple of weeks ago, I don't know if you recall my telling you that we used to have jam sessions up to Coleman Hawkins' house. (Inaudible)

Well, I would look forward to that more or less as a lesson for me because it was a great experience and all I did was play the chords for these giants. You know, and listen in. I realize now how much jazz came into my ear, you know, from these guys, you know, and --
